statement: Phase 2 has one sealed Docker Compose OCI host-runtime contract: the existing node-local lifecycle owner route targets one authenticated, label-scoped host agent without exposing Docker Engine authority to Lagrange nodes; artifact, operation, network, failure, cleanup, production-binding, and downstream live-proof boundaries are explicit, while Kubernetes remains a separate provider milestone.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

This Quest changes only architecture/oci-runtime-host-contract.md, architecture/INDEX.md, the active service-portability design alignment, its Oracle, and Quest evidence. It must not implement or modify a provider, host agent, Docker Compose service, runtime driver, feature gate, lifecycle reconciliation, endpoint publication, health, logs, or recovery behavior.

The terminal classification is selected_not_implemented: current realContainerActivation remains false, and only C1 may claim that shipped source reaches a real container through the selected binding.

The sealed route is the existing installed-service and node-local lifecycle ownership chain into RuntimeDriverRegistry, OciContainerDriver, one provider, and the host agent. The installation reconciler, CLI, SQL ingress, provider, and agent must not bypass or reproduce lifecycle, catalog, placement, service-instance, endpoint, or artifact-verification ownership.

Exactly one Docker Compose host agent per Docker Engine host is selected. Only the agent receives Docker Engine authority; Lagrange nodes and managed workloads receive neither the Docker socket nor a raw Engine API. The control transport, caller authentication, replay bound, redaction, operation allowlist, network/resource policy, and no-fallback behavior must be explicit.

C1 activation consumes an immutable remote OCI digest reference derived from the artifact-owner result. A host agent must never trust a CLI-supplied or node-local filesystem path; local OCI layouts require publication to an accessible registry before activation, and any future import protocol is a separate bounded decision.

The contract must define the versioned request/result grammar, deadlines, idempotency, typed failure and ambiguous-result semantics, mandatory agent-derived cluster/node/service/revision/instance labels, full-identity destructive checks, partial-create cleanup evidence, and restart/orphan posture. C1 owns pull/create/start/inspect/stop/remove; C2 extends the same envelope with probe/logs/endpoints/kill/replacement/recovery.

The sole selected production construction route is src/index.js through both seed and join options into createRuntimeStartupWiring and provider injection into OciContainerDriver. Demo-only, test-harness, direct-driver, buildx-exporter, direct Docker socket, provider auto-detection, and sequential provider fallback bindings are rejected.
Kubernetes, containerd, CRI, controller authority, and Kubernetes networking or privilege behavior are explicitly unsupported by this milestone and require a separate provider Quest.

The exact runner is node scripts/solve.js probe --probe oracle --file solve/oracle/oci-runtime-host-contract.json. Independent verification must inspect the architecture record, active design, current source evidence, and Oracle; removal of socket isolation, caller authentication, the canonical binding route, remote-digest rule, operation split, or Kubernetes exclusion must make the decision unapprovable.
